e:
Atrophic rhinitis (ozaena): greenish-black crusts, foul smell, merciful anosmia
Atrophic turbinates → roomy nasal cavity

Failed packing → endoscopic sphenopalatine artery ligation (most common surgical step)
ECA/ICA ligation less preferred
Mitomycin C (antifibrotic) applied topically in subglottic stenosis to ↓es scarring
Post-tonsillectomy (reactionary) bleed: take to OT, remove clot, ligate/cauterise bleeding point

Ring-enhancing lesion c̅ central hypodensity in temporal lobe = temporal lobe abscess
Common otogenic intracranial complication
Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) = sensory to oropharynx, tonsil, posterior 1/3 tongue

Circumvallate papilla: large dome-shaped, surrounded by a trench/moat
Taste buds on walls; von Ebner glands drain into the trench
Old trauma → frontal sinus obstruction → frontal mucocele c̅ bony erosion & non-axial proptosis
Permanent end-stoma c̅ no connection to upper airway = total laryngectomy
Rinne negative at 256 & 512 Hz but positive at 1024 Hz → AB gap 30–45 dB
Fossa of Rosenmüller (pharyngeal recess) behind torus tubarius = common site of nasopharyngeal Ca

Tracheostomy tube (outer, inner, obturator): airway toileting, bypass of upper airway obstruction, prolonged ventilation
Not for upper airway examination
Tonsil supplied by glossopharyngeal (IX) → referred otalgia via tympanic branch (Jacobson's nerve)

JNA: recurrent epistaxis + nasal obstruction
Holman–Miller sign = anterior bowing of posterior maxillary wall

Advanced laryngeal Ca c̅ subglottic extension + cartilage invasion → total laryngectomy
Partial laryngectomy only for early lesions
Central perforation c̅ air-bone gap & normal BC = conductive hearing loss (left ear)

Walsham forceps = closed reduction of nasal bone fracture
Asch forceps = septal reduction

CPA tumour c̅ unilateral SNHL + tinnitus = vestibular schwannoma
Antoni A (cellular, Verocay bodies) & Antoni B areas

Tubotympanic CSOM c̅ central perforation & conductive loss → myringoplasty (dry ear)
MRM is for atticoantral disease
Refractory anterior-superior septal bleeding → anterior ethmoidal artery ligation

HPV (esp. HPV-16) = most common cause of oropharyngeal SCC (base of tongue, tonsil)
EBV = nasopharyngeal Ca
Pyriform sinus: hypopharyngeal recess lateral to aryepiglottic fold; common site of hypopharyngeal Ca
